introduction_markdown:
**Cameroon General Certificate of Education Board - Ordinary Level Examination. Computer Science (0595), Paper 3 (practical), June 2023. Duration: two and a half hours. Do all the tasks (Task I, Task II and Task III) specified in the question paper.**

Enter the information required in the shaded boxes. For your guidance, the approximate mark for each part of a question is indicated in brackets. You are reminded of the necessity for good English and orderly presentation in your answers. In calculations, you are advised to show all the steps in your working, giving your answer at each stage. All written answers should be provided in the spaces provided in this question booklet. Calculators are NOT allowed.

The booklet reproduced here contains four versions of the same practical paper, headed Group One, Group Two, Group Three and Group Four (booklets 23/0595/3/Grp 1 to Grp 4); a candidate sits only ONE group. Each version has three tasks: Task I (word processing), Task II (spreadsheet) and Task III (a short exercise on HTML, on a database or on a C or Pascal program). The working files named in the tasks (the picture UN.jpg, the pictures of the authors) are supplied on the day; they are not reproduced in the printed paper.

questions.enonce_markdown:
Use the spreadsheet software on your computer to enter and format the information in Table 1. *[6 marks]*

Data to key in:

| Cell | Content | Cell | Content |
|---|---|---|---|
| B1 | Weekly Time Sheet | B14 | Regular Hourly Pay Rate |
| A3 | Employee Name: John Doe | C14 | 3,500 |
| A4 | Week: 7 - 11 February 2018 | B15 | Overtime Hourly Pay Rate |
| A6:D6 | S/N, Day, Hrs Worked, Cum Hours | B17 | Hours for the Week |
| A7:C7 | 1, Monday, 10 | B18 | Overtime Hours |
| A8:C8 | 2, Tuesday, 9.5 | B19 | Regular Hours |
| A9:C9 | 3, Wednesday, 10 | B21 | Regular Pay for the Week |
| A10:C10 | 4, Thursday, 7.5 | B22 | Overtime Pay for the Week |
| A11:C11 | 5, Friday, 8.5 | B23 | Total Pay for the Week |
questions.corrige_markdown:
1. Open a new workbook in the spreadsheet.
2. Key in the title, the employee name, the week and the table headings in the cells shown (the row and column labels of the figure are the cell addresses).
3. Key in the five days with their serial number and the hours worked (10, 9.5, 10, 7.5, 8.5) in column C, and the label cells of the lower blocks (B14, B15, B17 to B19, B21 to B23). Key in the regular hourly pay rate 3500 in C14.
4. Format as in the figure: title in bold and centred over the table, bold headings, borders around the three blocks, labels on the right (right-aligned), a thousands separator in C14 so that it reads 3,500.
5. Leave empty the cells that will receive formulas (D7:D11, C15, C17:C19, C21:C23).

Marking idea (6 marks): title, name and week (1); table headings and the five days (1); hours worked correct (1); labels of the lower blocks (1); rate 3,500 (1); formatting (borders, bold, alignment) (1).

questions.enonce_markdown: Add the following formula to Cell D7: =C7. What does the formula compute? *[1 mark]*
questions.corrige_markdown:
In D7 type `=C7`. The formula copies the number of hours worked on Monday (cell C7). Because Monday is the first day, this is the **cumulative number of hours up to Monday**, which is simply Monday's hours: **10**.

Marking idea (1 mark): the cumulative hours for Monday (= the hours worked on Monday, 10).

questions.enonce_markdown: Enter in Cell D8, a formula that computes the sum of the cumulative total for Monday and the hours worked on Tuesday. Write the formula you entered in the space below. *[2 marks]*
questions.corrige_markdown:
The cumulative total for Monday is in D7 and the hours worked on Tuesday are in C8, so

**D8: `=D7+C8`**

Check: $10 + 9.5 = 19.5$ hours. Each day's cumulative total is the previous day's cumulative total plus that day's hours.

Marking idea (2 marks): D7 used (1); C8 added (1).

questions.enonce_markdown: Copy the formula in (c) above to the cell range D9:D11. *[1 mark]*
questions.corrige_markdown:
Select D8, drag the fill handle down to D11 (or copy D8 and paste in D9:D11). The references move down with the formula (`=D8+C9`, `=D9+C10`, `=D10+C11`).

Results for D7 to D11 (Cum Hours):

| Row | Day | Hrs Worked | Cum Hours |
|---|---|---|---|
| 7 | Monday | 10 | 10 |
| 8 | Tuesday | 9.5 | 19.5 |
| 9 | Wednesday | 10 | 29.5 |
| 10 | Thursday | 7.5 | 37 |
| 11 | Friday | 8.5 | 45.5 |

Marking idea (1 mark): formula copied down to D11 with correct values.

questions.enonce_markdown: The overtime hourly pay rate is 1.5 times the regular hourly pay rate. Enter a formula in Cell C15 to compute the overtime hourly pay rate. Write the formula you entered in the space below. *[2 marks]*
questions.corrige_markdown:
The regular rate is in C14, so

**C15: `=C14*1.5`**

Result: $3500 \times 1.5 = 5250$.

Marking idea (2 marks): reference to C14 (1); multiplication by 1.5 (1).

questions.enonce_markdown: Enter a formula in Cell C17 that inserts the Cumulative Hours up to Friday into Cell C17. *[1 mark]*
questions.corrige_markdown:
The cumulative hours up to Friday are in D11, so

**C17: `=D11`**

Result: **45.5** hours for the week (check: $10 + 9.5 + 10 + 7.5 + 8.5 = 45.5$). `=SUM(C7:C11)` gives the same value.

Marking idea (1 mark): `=D11` (or an equivalent formula) giving 45.5.

questions.enonce_markdown: Using the IF function; enter a formula in Cell C18 that computes overtime hours. If the hours worked for the week is greater than 40, overtime hours is computed as hours for the week - 40; otherwise overtime hours is 0. Write the formula you typed in the space below. *[3 marks]*
questions.corrige_markdown:
The hours for the week are in C17. The test is "greater than 40":

**C18: `=IF(C17>40,C17-40,0)`**

Here $45.5 > 40$ is true, so the overtime hours are $45.5 - 40 = 5.5$. If the week had 40 hours or fewer, the formula would give 0.

Marking idea (3 marks): IF function with the condition C17>40 (1); value if true C17-40 (1); value if false 0 (1).

questions.enonce_markdown: Enter in cell C19, the formula for regular hours (hours for the week - overtime hours). *[1 mark]*
questions.corrige_markdown:
**C19: `=C17-C18`**

Result: $45.5 - 5.5 = 40$ regular hours.

Marking idea (1 mark): `=C17-C18`.

questions.enonce_markdown: Enter appropriate formulas for cells C12, C22 and C23. *[3 marks]*
questions.corrige_markdown:
The printed question says "C12", but row 12 is an empty row of the sheet: the three result cells of the pay block are **C21** (Regular Pay for the Week), C22 and C23, so the formulas are entered there:

- **C21** (regular pay): **`=C19*C14`** = $40 \times 3500 = 140000$.
- **C22** (overtime pay): **`=C18*C15`** = $5.5 \times 5250 = 28875$.
- **C23** (total pay): **`=C21+C22`** = $140000 + 28875 = 168875$.

(The answers are in the same currency unit as the pay rate of 3,500 per hour.)

Marking idea (3 marks): one mark for each correct formula (regular pay, overtime pay, total pay).
